## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Shànsī tóngzǐ jīng* (T479) is a two-fascicle Sui translation parallel to *Fóshuō dàfāngděng dǐngwáng jīng* [KR6i0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0106) and *Dàchéng dǐngwáng jīng* [KR6i0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0107) of the *Mūrdharāja-sūtra* tradition. The protagonist *Shànsī tóngzǐ* 善思童子 ("Boy of Good Reflection") is the same figure as *Dǐngwáng* 頂王 ("Crowned-King") of the earlier translations — [闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) Jñānagupta has rendered the Sanskrit name differently. The Taishō header cross-references Nos. 477 and 478.

**Abstract**

This is the third and most polished Chinese translation of the *Mūrdharāja-sūtra*. Jñānagupta's translation is dated to his Sui productive period (591–600 CE). The two-fascicle expansion (compared with the one-fascicle earlier translations) suggests Jñānagupta worked from a more complete *Vorlage* than was available to [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) Dharmarakṣa or [月婆首那](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%88%E5%A9%86%E9%A6%96%E9%82%A3) Yuèpó Shǒunà.

The narrative tells of the bodhisattva career of Vimalakīrti's son, but Jñānagupta's translation tradition associates the figure with specific Yogācāra doctrinal content, possibly reflecting a later layer of Indic editing that emphasized *vijñaptimātra*-style readings.
